newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks move on thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks move on thin trade.

text.p: Cyprus stocks edged lower in the week without any signs of company "window dressing" that brokers expected this time of year.
The 41-share general index of the CSE slid 0.42 percent to 81.48 at the end of a week's trading on Friday. Last week the index closed at 81.83 points.
Many brokers had expected shares to go up as the end of the year approached as part of the "window dressing" tactic adopted by some companies -- whereby they buy up their shares to prop up the price.
"Investors seem disinterested in stocks of the secondary market," said CISCO stockbrokers in their weekly report, which pointed out new equity and bond issues this year had been sucessful.
Banking stocks closed at 90.44 on Friday, up slightly from last week's close of 90.20, with few significant changes in the prices of shares.
Bank of Cyprus fully paid shares slid two cents to close at 339.5 from 341.5 last week. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank went up 5.5 cents, closing at 327.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares closed at 256.5 shedding three cents from their closing price last week, while shares in the Universal Savings Bank lost 5.5 cents, closing at 134.5.
National carrier Cyprus Airways scored three year-lows during the week, on Wednesday at 0.376, on Thursday at 0.375 and on Friday at 0.372 in thin trade.

A parliamentary debate on the future of the airline, which is 80 percent state owned, was postponed on Friday. The parliamentary finance committee is now due to to look at future strategies of the airline during a meeting on January 15.

The insurance companies sub index closed at 56.13 on Friday from 57.22 last week. Universal Life UNII.CY insurance closed at 374.5 from 379.5 last week. Interamerican shed 1.5 cents, closing at 100.5.
Vassiliko Cement was trading at 162.5, slipping six cents from last week's close.
